NEUROLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-08-16
30M, ambulatory follow-up visit in neurology clinic.

S:
Patient returns for scheduled neurology follow-up and review of his breathing regimen. He reports that his mobility has been stable but that fatigue in the legs limits how long he can stand at work. He uses his rescue inhaler a few times a week, mostly with exertion and dust exposure. He works part time in a mailroom sorting parcels. He could not complete 8 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. Patient denies depression. Sleep is adequate. Diet is high in sugary drinks, which was discussed. Lives with his parents, who help with transport. Never smoker.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 76, RR 15, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 158 lb, BMI 23.
General: alert, pleasant, in no acute distress.
Neuro: spastic gait, uses a walker for distances, strength 4/5 in lower extremities, normal upper extremity tone.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally today, good air movement.
Labs (this week): A1c 6.1%, basic metabolic panel within normal limits.

A/P:
1. Cerebral palsy, ambulates with a walker. Continue physical therapy twice weekly and home stretching. Reassessed walker fit; referral to physiatry for a gait evaluation. Reviewed fall-prevention strategies at home and work.
2. Asthma, uncomplicated, using inhaler as needed. Inhaler technique reviewed and found adequate; continue short-acting reliever before exertion. Provided a written action plan and advised a dust mask during sorting.
3. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Discussed swapping sugary drinks for water and adding seated resistance work. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
4. Function and work: current limits are affecting his ability to keep a full schedule. Provided a letter describing activity restrictions for his employer.

Return to clinic in 3 months, sooner if mobility or breathing changes.
